title: The son of Sky and the hidden rivers

plan.english: The great serpent lay on the mountain, and it was hiding the rivers inside. The earth was thirsty and the cattle were thirsty. Then the gods spoke to the hero: "Slay the serpent! Free them!" He took his spear and went forward. The serpent saw him coming. He slew the serpent. He split the mountain apart. The rivers came forth, and the earth drank the water. The gods gave imperishable fame to him.

The cattle of the gods were on the hill. When it was getting dark there, a snake stole the cattle and drove them into the mountain. When Dawn became bright, they sought the cattle. A god said: "Our cattle are gone! Who stole them?" Then a man said: "A snake stole them. I shall seek out the cattle." He arrived at the mountain, and split it open. The snake became afraid. Then he killed the snake. The cattle came forth. May Father Sky, giver of good things, guard the cattle!

title: The two sons of Sky and the Sun's daughter

plan.english: The daughter of the Sun went to the water. The water was great, and she sank down in it. She became afraid, and she said: "Hear me, O two sons of Sky! Free me from the water!" They heard her. They arrived on a chariot, and two swift horses carried it. They drew her out of the water and set her on the chariot. Then they led her to the Sun. He became glad, and he said: "You have freed my daughter! Protect men!"

Dawn, the daughter of Sky, becomes bright. She makes the path straight for the Sun. Then he climbs the sky. Seven swift yoked horses carry his chariot. His daughter sits on it. From above he looks at the earth and the cattle. Mortals see him, and they become glad. When it is getting dark there, he goes down into the waters. His swift horses become tired. Then Dawn becomes bright again. O Dawn, daughter of Sky, make the path straight for us!

title: How Sky and Earth were parted

plan.english: Sky lay on Earth. Men lived in between, and it was getting dark there. A man became strong. He stood up, and pushed them apart. Sky was above, and Earth was below. Then it became bright above, and they looked around. "Father Sky, Mother Earth, hear us!" They heard us.

Fire went away from the gods, and sank down into the waters. They were seeking him. "Where is Fire?" Fire was red. A large fish saw him in the water and spoke: "He is in the waters." They went to the waters, and they said: "O Fire, come forth! We shall set a famous name for you." Fire came forth from the water. They seized him and led him to the mortals. Now mortals cook with fire. O Fire, giver of good things, protect us!

A mortal lay down on the earth. Death arrived at his side, and he died. His brother saw him lying down, and he became afraid. He said to the gods: "He is lying flat, and he does not see me." They said: "Mortals die. Death comes to men. Good fame does not vanish." They set a famous name for him. Then his name became great.

title: The she-wolf and the two sons of the king

plan.english: The brother of the king seized the two sons, and laid them down on the earth. Then he went away. A she-wolf heard them, came to them, and nourished them. A shepherd saw them. The two grew up and became strong. They spoke to the shepherd: "Who is our father?" He said: "The king is your father. His brother seized you." The two went to him and killed him. The two became famous.

Dawn, driving the red cattle, comes from the mountain. The mortals wake up. The dogs listen to her, and the wolves go away. The shepherd leads his sheep forward. They drink the water. She gives them good things. Short is her path. The Sun looks at her, and she leaves. "O Dawn, daughter of Sky, drive the red cattle to us! Hear us!"

The Sun gave his daughter to the hero, and gave him ten cattle. Now he became the son-in-law of the Sun. He led two swift horses. They carried the chariot, and she sat on it. His mother saw her. The mother said: "O daughter, be dear to me! Be the wife of my son!" "I shall be a wife." May the gods protect the two, and may the two live!

The king arrived at the river, driving his cattle. It was swelling. He spoke to it: "O river, be passable for my cattle!" "Do not be afraid, O king! I shall be passable." He went through it, and the cattle followed him. On the other side he gave three cattle to the river. Then he sat down. The river became glad. It is great.

A serpent seized the sister of four brothers, and led her inside. Three brothers entered the mountain, and the serpent killed them. The serpent was long. The fourth stood at the mountain. He said: "O serpent, come forth!" The serpent came forth, and he slew the serpent. Then he went in, and freed his sister. He led her out. Great fame came to him.

title: The broken wheel of the Sun

plan.english: The Sun burned the fields. The rivers dried up, and the cattle became thirsty. Then a hero went to the Sun. He broke the wheel of the Sun. The horses trembled. Dawn spoke to him: "What have you done?" "I have done this. The cattle were thirsty." The Sun built a wheel again, and the horses carried it.

title: The two dogs at the river

plan.english: A mortal died. He went along the path, and arrived at the river. Two dogs with four eyes were lying there. They saw him, and he said: "O dogs, let me go!" They heard his name. They let him go. He went through the river, and came to the gods. They gave him good things.

The gods sat down on the mountain. Father Sky spoke: "Who will protect the mortals?" Dawn said: "I shall protect them." The earth said: "I shall protect them from below." Fire said: "I shall protect them in the field." "Good is your word." Mother Earth heard them, and she became glad. They drank sweet water.

A king arrived at the gods. He said: "O gods, may I not die!" They said: "Mortals die. Death comes to the king and to the shepherd." "Then give me imperishable fame!" They gave it to him. Death came to him, and he died. His fame did not vanish. Men say his name.

title: The raid on the cattle of the queen

plan.english: The hero stole the cattle of the queen, and drove them away. The shepherds saw him driving the cattle, and went to the queen. They said: "He stole our cattle!" The queen said to the warriors: "Seize your spears! Follow him!" They followed him. Then he reached the river and drove the cattle through it. They arrived at the river, and became afraid. He stood on the other side and said: "Whoever seeks the cattle, let him come through it!" They did not come. He drove them to his field. Imperishable fame went to him.

The hero and the other man arrived at the field. They stood opposite one another. The other man said: "Who are you?" "I am the son of the king. Whoever is afraid, let him go away!" The other man let go his spear, and the spear passed by him. Then he let go his spear, and the spear bored through the heart of the other man. He fell down, and died. He took the two horses of the other man and drove them away. Imperishable fame arose for him.

The queen said to the men: "Whoever drives his horses to the hill, to him I shall give ten cattle." The hill was far away. Two swift yoked horses carried the chariot of the hero. Two horses carried the chariot of the other man. The two went forward. "Swift horses, carry me! Do not become tired!" The two horses listened to him, and the chariot of the other man broke. He fell down. The hero reached the hill. The queen gave him ten cattle. Good fame went to him.

title: The death of the king's son

plan.english: There was a great fight. The son of the king killed the warriors. Then a spear bored through his heart. He fell down, and died. His two horses stood beside him. The king heard the word, and arrived there. He saw him lying down. The wife came. She said: "O husband, you are gone! My heart trembles. Who will protect me?" "You went away from your father. Death seized you." May his fame not vanish! May his fame be imperishable!

title: The two paths of the hero

plan.english: The mother of the hero spoke to him: "Two paths are yours. On the long path you will live, and your name will vanish. On the short path you will die, and imperishable fame will be yours." "I shall go on the short path." "Do not go, my son!" "Let me go, mother!" He led his two horses to the fight. Then a spear bored through his heart. He lay down, and died. His mother said: "He is gone, and his fame did not vanish."

A serpent lay on the hill, and it devoured the cattle of the queen. The queen said to the warriors: "Who will slay the serpent?" They became afraid. A man stood up and said: "I shall slay the serpent." "If you slay the serpent, I shall give you my daughter." He went forward. The serpent saw him coming. He slew the serpent. The queen gave him her daughter. Great fame went to him.

The hero drove his two horses to the fight. The left horse stood. It spoke to him: "We shall carry you away from the fight. Death is near you." "I know it, horse. Death is near me. Carry me to the fight, swift horses!" The two horses carried him to the fight. Then a spear bored through his heart, and he fell from the chariot. Imperishable fame went to him.

title: The vengeance of the king's son

plan.english: Warriors killed the king. His son grew up, and became strong. He spoke to his mother: "Whoever killed my father, to him I shall give punishment." He drove his two horses to them. They saw him coming. He struck them down. They fell down, and he gave them punishment. Then he became king. His fame became great.

When it was getting dark on the hill, the warriors lay down on the earth. The hero was awake. He heard the wolves, and the wolves came forward. He spoke to them: "Wake up, warriors! Seize your spears!" They woke up. A wolf seized a sheep. They killed the wolves. The she-wolf went away. It became bright above. He looked around. The sheep were alive.

title: The two brothers on the chariot

plan.english: The hero and his brother went to the fight on a chariot. His brother drove the two swift horses. They arrived at the warriors. He struck them. Another man let go his spear, and the spear bored through the heart of the brother. He fell down from the chariot. Then he seized them, and drove them forward. Then he carried him away from the fight. He said: "My brother, you are gone! Your fame will not vanish."

The wife was sitting on the hill. She was looking at the path. The years went by. Her heart trembled. She spoke: "O Dawn, bring my husband! You see the fields and the waters. Do you see him?" "I see him. He is coming along the path." The wife saw him coming. She knew him, and her heart became glad. He reached her. The two became glad.

Men laid the hero down. They burned him with fire. The fire was red. His father stood by the fire. His wife looked at the fire. He said to them: "Set a famous name for him!" They set a famous name for him. Then he gave them ten cattle. Imperishable fame is his. Death took him, and his fame did not vanish.

The hero and the warrior stood opposite one another. The warrior said: "You are a wolf. You steal cattle. Your heart is the heart of a sheep!" "Your words are sweet, and your spear is short. My spear is long." The warrior said: "Come through the river!" Then a mortal came between them. He spoke: "Go away from it, both of you!" Then the two went away.

title: The track of the two horses

plan.english: When it was getting dark on the hill, another man stole the two horses of the hero. When Dawn became bright, the hero sought his two horses. He tracked them, and arrived at the mountain. He saw him sitting. He said: "Who are you?" The other man stood up. The hero struck him down, and he fell down. Then he led the two horses away.

For ten years the man worked in a far field. The years were long. Then he came to his own hill. A dog was lying there. The dog saw him, and knew him. It came to him, and died. His wife was sitting there. He came to her. She did not know him. He said: "Wife, do you not know me?" "I know you." The two became glad.

The hero drove the warriors to the river. He killed them in the river. It was swelling. The water came against him. He became afraid, and said: "O Fire, free me from the water!" Fire came, and dried it. It went away. He stood up on the hill. He said: "O Fire, giver of good things, you have freed me!"

Warriors seized the queen, and drove her and the cattle away. The brother of the queen said to the hero: "Free her! I shall give you a great prize." He tracked them. He arrived at the mountain, and saw them sitting. He killed them. The queen saw him, and he freed her. He drove them away, and led her to her brother, who gave him the prize. Imperishable fame went to him.

title: The words of the father to his son

plan.english: The father spoke to his son: "Hear my words. Guard the cattle and the sheep. Do not steal the cattle of another. Whoever seeks fame, let him be good. Death comes to men. Do not become afraid, my son!" He heard them, and said: "I shall do so." He became great, and his name became famous.

A wolf met a dog. The wolf said: "O dog, you eat sweet things." The dog said: "Come with me, wolf! The shepherd gives sweet things to you." "Does he let you go away?" "He did not let me go." "I shall not go with you. I am free." The wolf went away, and he sat down. The free become glad, and the yoked do not become glad.

A wolf and a sheep came to the river. The wolf stood above, and the sheep stood below. She drank the water. The wolf said: "Who is drinking my water?" "I am drinking the water below you." "Last year you spoke words against me!" "Last year I did not speak." "Then your father spoke!" The wolf seized the sheep, and devoured her. The wolf finds words, and the sheep finds death.

title: The wolf and the heel of the horse

plan.english: A wolf saw a horse. The wolf said: "I shall devour you, horse." The horse said: "Look at my heel, wolf! Then devour me!" The wolf came near, and looked at the heel of the horse. The horse struck the wolf with the heel. The wolf fell down, and said: "Sweet were the words of the horse, and the heel of the horse struck me." Whoever trusts sweet words, death finds him.

In winter a snake lay down. The snake became cold. A shepherd saw the snake, and seized it. He warmed it with fire. The snake became warm. Then the snake seized him. He said: "I warmed you with fire, and do you seize me?" "I am a snake." Then it killed him. Do not warm a snake! Whoever warms a snake, the snake will kill him.

A shepherd drove his sheep to the hill. He spoke: "The wolf is coming!" Men came forward. They did not see a wolf. The shepherd became glad. Again he said: "The wolf is coming!" They came again. They were not glad. Then a wolf came forward. The shepherd said: "The wolf is coming! Come to us!" They heard him, and they did not come. The wolf seized them, and devoured them. "My words were not good."

The she-wolf said to her son: "Do not go to the field of the sheep! A dog is in it. It hears well, and the spear of the shepherd is long." He said: "I am not afraid." He went there. The dog heard him, and the shepherd was grasping his spear. He killed him. The she-wolf said: "My son, you did not hear my words." Whoever does not hear the words of his mother, death comes to him.
